    - "Emphasise whole, minimally processed foods."

    - "Regular high-fiber carbohydrates: vegetables, fruits, whole grains."

    - "Include greens and colourful vegetables daily."

    - "Prioritise hydration: 2-2.5L water daily (adjust for activity)."
    - "Evening meals: lighter, balanced to aid sleep and digestion."
    - "During flow or flare days: reduce high-intensity effort, focus on easily digestible meals and gentle hydration."
  SAMPLE_MEALS:
    - "Breakfast: oats with berries, ground flaxseed, chopped nuts, and a drizzle of olive oil or tahini."
    - "Lunch: mixed leafy salad with grilled salmon or chickpeas, quinoa, avocado, olive oil dressing."
    - "Snack: Greek yogurt or dairy-free alternative with turmeric and cinnamon, handful of walnuts."
    - "Dinner: baked white fish or lentil stew, steamed vegetables, sweet potato, side of sautéed greens with garlic and olive oil."
    - "Snack option: hummus with carrot and cucumber sticks or a piece of fruit."
  SUPPLEMENT_SUGGESTIONS:
    - "Consider omega-3 (fish oil) 1-2g EPA+DHA daily after consulting healthcare provider."
    - "Vitamin D if deficient per blood test."
    - "Avoid initiating new supplements during flare without medical approval."
  CYCLING_ADJUSTMENTS:
    - "Menstrual flow days and reported flare windows (2026-07-10 to 13, 2026-08-04 to 07): avoid plyometric and high-impact sessions; replace with low-impact alternatives (walking, cycling, rowing) and focus on gentle mobility and nutrition."
    - "On these days, favour simple proteins (poached fish, eggs, tofu), cooked vegetables, bone broth or warming soups, small frequent meals."
    - "Maintain anti-inflammatory staples (berries, leafy greens, oily fish) and hydration."

    - "Cook in batches: soups, stews, grain salads for easy flare-day meals."
    - "Use anti-inflammatory spices: turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, garlic."
    - "Limit alcohol and excess caffeine especially around flare and flow days."
    - "Track symptoms against foods to identify personal triggers."
    - "Perform plyometric sessions and 1RM testing only outside flow and known flare windows; if any pelvic or abdominal pain occurs, stop and switch to low-impact power drills (fast marching, high-knee marching)."
